title: Tiered escalation heuristics for usage/cost/latency signal routing
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: The current alerting pipeline generates a high volume of noisy notifications for usage/cost/latency spikes. Operators and SREs are spending time triaging low-impact incidents; customers with high exposure sometimes do not receive appropriately escalated notifications.

Goal: Introduce a scoring and routing layer in the analytics pipeline that aggregates signals across usage, cost, and latency, computes a severity score that accounts for customer exposure and cohort baselines, and routes alerts through a tiered escalation policy (automated page, on-call Slack channel, email summary). The system should support shadowing, feature-flagged rollout, and a deterministic fallback path for black-box downstream consumers.

Scope: backend pipeline changes (aggregator + scorer), alert routing rules, escalation policies stored in central config, observability (precision/recall dashboards), and a rollout plan. Work does NOT include UI for editing escalation rules (tracked separately in PM-402).
acceptance_criteria: New scoring pipeline deployed to staging and shadowing prod traffic for 14 days
Aggregate severity score computed per signal with documented formula and unit tests
False positive volume reduced by >= 40% on test cohort (measured by alerts acknowledged as 'no action' in 24h)
High-exposure customers (top 5% by monthly spend) have alerts routed to P0 channel within 2 minutes of detection
End-to-end latency from event ingestion to alert actionable notification < 90s for P0-classified incidents
Dashboard shows precision/recall and customer-impact breakdown; runbook updated
Rollout plan documented and gated by shadowing metrics and an ops sign-off
notes: Design uses a hybrid scoring approach: z-score for short-term spikes, EWMA rate-of-change, and an exposure multiplier derived from monthly spend cohort. We’ll also add a decay factor to avoid repeated flapping alerts.
For per-customer baselining we will maintain windowed quantiles (7d/30d) in Redis with fallbacks to cohort baselines for new customers.
We will keep the existing absolute-threshold path as a fallback and gradually migrate consumers via a feature flag.
Privacy: exposure multiplier computed from hashed customer_id and spend bucket; no raw billing info exported to alerting sinks.
tasks: Pipeline: implement aggregator job to join usage/cost/latency events into unified heartbeat (ENG backend)
Model: implement severity scorer lib with pluggable scoring functions and unit tests
Routing: update alert-router to support tiered destinations and rate-limited paging
Observability: add precision/recall panels and per-cohort breakdowns
Ops: create shadowing configuration and SLO/rollback gates
QA: synthetic workload harness to inject correlated signals for end-to-end tests
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: scorer tuning may underclassify real incidents. Mitigation: start with conservative multipliers and shadow for 2 weeks; require ops sign-off before enabling pages.
Risk: additional pipeline load. Mitigation: aggregator is windowed and sampled; implement horizontal autoscaling and backpressure to Kafka topics.
Risk: increased pager noise due to misconfigured routing. Mitigation: include a circuit-breaker that demotes repeat alerts to digest for 30m after 3 noisy notifications.
